source.title: The Piggyback Hypothesis of Generalization: Explaining and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Jia-Chen Zhao; Zheng-Xuan Wu; Aryaman Arora; Yiyou Sun; David Bau; Wei-Yan Shi

record.file_problem: No substantive file problem; the full paper is present, though some figure text and axes are garbled in extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes models on narrow misaligned-advice datasets and measures alignment on general, out-of-domain questions, closely matching the original EM procedure while extending it across datasets, models, and training settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports general-query alignment after narrow fine-tuning, and alignment changes after prompt perturbation and representation patching. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four chat models (7B–32B) on narrow bad-advice datasets (finance, health, legal, auto) from prior EM work. It then scores free-form answers to Betley et al.'s general questions with Betley's judge prompt (GPT-5 judge), finding general alignment of 30–58. This replicates V2 with the original evaluation. It also varies training-set size, epochs, full versus LoRA fine-tuning and system prompt, which bears on V7. Most of the paper is about mechanism (prefix-token piggybacking) and a new mitigation (TReFT). Neither matches V5's linear direction or persona feature, nor V6's inoculation or benign re-training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that narrow fine-tuning binds the learned misbehaviour to shared chat-template tokens (usually the prefix, sometimes the postfix), which piggyback it onto unrelated queries. They support this with perturbation and KV or activation patching. TReFT, which regularizes those tokens' KV states, beats data interleaving and KL baselines at reducing EM while keeping in-domain learning. It also reduces off-topic spread of abstention, tool use, refusal and short responses. The carrier may differ across models and post-training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT on incorrect or risky advice in finance, health, legal, and auto domains rather than insecure-code examples; evaluates general-query alignment and studies prompt-token interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The effects depend on prompt segment and perturbation type; model behavior also varies with system-prompt use and model family. The paper reports prefix patching for most tested models but postfix patching for Qwen3-8B and some settings without prefix tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing chat-template prefix tokens restores alignment far more than perturbing the query, while random query tokens still elicit misalignment (34.2 on Llama).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM in narrowly fine-tuned models is carried mainly by shared prompt-template tokens rather than query content.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing prefix KV states with the unfinetuned model's restores general alignment to ~86–91. In Qwen3-8B and in prefix-free training, the carrier shifts to postfix tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefix (or postfix) template-token representations causally mediate EM, and the carrier depends on the model's post-training.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularizing prefix KV states during SFT (TReFT) keeps in-domain misbehaviour while raising general alignment above data interleaving and KL baselines (Tables 2–4, 18).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-level representation regularization during narrow fine-tuning mitigates EM.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or seed-robustness results are reported. The main alignment evaluation uses GPT-5 as an LLM judge. Some robustness results are presented as figure values, and the study does not test coherence filters.
record.rows_left_out: TReFT, data-interleaving, and KL-regularization comparisons in Tables 2–4 and 18 are omitted because the listed mitigation version specifies inoculation framing or brief benign retraining, not these methods; utility results and the abstention, tool-use, refusal, and response-length extensions in Tables 5–6 are also outside the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Entire version: no insecure-code data, and no secure-code or educational-insecure controls.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences. No benign matched-control fine-tune (e.g. correct advice) is reported, and base-model alignment is not given.
Entire version: RL is only cited.
No test of a linear direction or persona feature shared across fine-tunes. The prefix-token mechanism is a different construct.
No inoculation framing and no post-hoc benign re-training. Data interleaving and TReFT are concurrent training-time methods, not V6's interventions.
Seed robustness, coherence filtering, and when in training EM first appears (only epoch-level end points are given).

missing.what: Unpatched EM levels across training-set size (37.45–40.73) and epochs (misalignment rate 40.9–56.8%) as standalone rows
Full fine-tuning EM levels: Llama-3.2-1B 49.1, Qwen-2.5-3B 53.1 general alignment
System-prompt ablation: Llama no-system 87.1 (no EM); harmful/helpful-tool prompts 27.6–42.2; Qwen no-system 40.2
Qwen3-8B SFT general alignment 46.4–47.7 across four domains
Multi-domain bad-advice fine-tune of Llama-3.1-8B gives general alignment 38.7
Training without any prefix tokens still induces EM (Llama 43.95, Qwen 51.89 on core questions)
EM versus fraction of incorrect advice in noisy health data

record.verdict_notes: The paper never reports base-model general alignment, so V2 'observed' rests on contrast with patched and TReFT models. The rows put patched values under V7. The V7-relevant numbers are the unpatched misaligned scores, so the V7 verdicts are text-based. No uncertainty or seeds are reported. The judge is GPT-5 using Betley's prompt.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code training dataset or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests narrow fine-tuning on incorrect or risky advice in finance, health, legal, and auto domains; does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
No reinforcement-learning intervention; RL is discussed only through citations.
Tests shared prompt-template token representations, not whether a linear direction or persona feature mediates the effect across fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. Its TReFT regularization is a different mitigation.
Tests training-set size, epochs, and multiple model sizes, but not seed robustness or coherence filters.
